○ trial-6z4 · Quote a monthly statement total   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Add total for a complete monthly statement. Request:                        
  {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} with optional release "1.0". Return  
  exactly release, credit_cents, and amount_due_cents for the whole charge set
  under the approved release agreement. The total must reflect that           
  agreement's credit-cap scope across the supplied lines. It is not a         
  collection of independent single-line quote requests. Keep quote available. 
                                                                              
  An empty statement returns                                                  
  {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. A statement        
  containing only the line in the quote example returns {"release": "1.0",    
  "credit_cents": 1999, "amount_due_cents": 18000}.
✓ Updated issue: trial-6z4 — Quote a monthly statement total

Meridian Credits release 1.0: Finance-approved initial credit agreement and CLI contract. Source: issue trial-5j0, "Quote a single renewal charge", description (2026-09-07). This record preserves the complete approved agreement, including multi-line rules beyond the single-line feature implemented in trial-5j0; those broader rules are approval, not a claim of implemented multi-line support.

Protocol and scope: Python standard-library local CLI, python3 main.py, accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON object on stdout. No network, clock, locale, or third-party package is needed. Malformed input is outside these issues. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and existing unknown command response {"error":"unknown_command"}. JSON object key order is immaterial; response keys must be exactly those specified.

Data contract: Each charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, charge_cents. IDs are nonempty strings, with line_id unique within a request. Subscription identity is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription_id can recur under different accounts and each subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31 inclusive. charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID ordering means Unicode code-point order.

Approved release 1.0 calculation: Compute each line's uncapped credit as 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by every line with the same account_id across its subscriptions; distinct account groups have independent caps. Within each cap group, allocate credit by earliest service_on, then increasing line_id for equal dates. Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the remaining group cap; later lines receive the remainder or zero. Total credit is the sum of assigned line credits. Line amount due equals charge minus assigned credit; total due equals total charges minus total credit.

Version policy: Release "1.0" is the initial and currently selected agreement as introduced by trial-5j0. Omitting release selects the current agreement; explicit supported releases select that version. Introduced versions remain supported afterward. Public suites use explicit releases so their expectations survive current-agreement changes; run python3 test_public.py --cases PATH. No unsupported-release behavior was specified.

Single-line quote API introduced by trial-5j0: {"command":"quote","line":LINE}, optionally with "release":"1.0". Treat the line as the entire statement. Response contains exactly release ("1.0"), line_id copied from the input, credit_cents, and amount_due_cents. Example: charge 19999 -> credit 1999 and amount due 18000. Implementation verified with the supplied public_tests/release_1_quote.json suite and unittest checks covering ping, unknown commands, default/explicit release, zero/sub-cent rounding, the cap boundary, large integer charges, Unicode line IDs, and both allowed service-date endpoints.

  Example response: {"release": "1.0", "credit_cents": 1999,                  
  "amount_due_cents": 18000, "line_id": "L-1"}

Close one or more issues.

If no issue ID is provided, closes the last touched issue (from most recent
create, update, show, or close operation). This fallback only applies in
interactive sessions (stdin is a terminal); in scripts and agent sessions a
missing ID is an error, so a command built from an empty variable cannot
silently close an unrelated issue. Set BD_LAST_TOUCHED_FALLBACK=1 to allow
the fallback anywhere, or =0 to disable it entirely.

When closing multiple issues, provide one --reason for all IDs or repeat
--reason once per ID. Reasons map positionally: the first --reason applies
to the first ID, the second --reason to the second ID, regardless of where
the flags appear in the command line.

Usage:
  bd close [id...] [flags]

Aliases:
  close, done

Flags:
      --claim-next           Automatically claim the next highest priority available issue
      --continue             Auto-advance to next step in molecule
  -f, --force                Force close pinned issues or unsatisfied gates
  -h, --help                 help for close
      --no-auto              With --continue, show next step but don't claim it
  -r, --reason string        Reason for closing
      --reason-file string   Read close reason from file (use - for stdin)
      --session string       Claude Code session ID (or set CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env var)
      --suggest-next         Show newly unblocked issues after closing

Global Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)
      --cpu-profile               Generate CPU profile for performance analysis
      --database string           Run against a different server database for this invocation, without changing the project's configured database (proxied-server mode only)
      --db string                 Database path (default: auto-discover .beads/*.db). In proxied-server mode, a value that isn't an existing path is treated as a database name override (see --database)
  -C, --directory string          Change to this directory before running the command (like git -C)
      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then (a live batch-mode bd process also flushes on SIGTERM/SIGHUP). Applies to embedded and direct SQL-server modes; proxied-server routes are unaffected. Default: on. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit
      --global                    Use the global shared-server database (beads_global)
      --ignore-schema-skew        Proceed despite forward schema drift (some queries may fail)
      --json                      Output in JSON format
      --mem-profile string        Write heap profile to FILE on exit (also respects BEADS_MEM_PROFILE)
      --no-color                  Disable color output (also: NO_COLOR=1 or CLICOLOR=0)
  -q, --quiet                     Suppress non-essential output (errors only)
      --readonly                  Read-only mode: block write operations (for worker sandboxes)
      --sandbox                   Sandbox mode: disables Dolt auto-push
  -v, --verbose                   Enable verbose/debug output
